To calculate the percentage by which NFA-A fell behind NCA after 100 cycles, we need to first determine the capacity retention of NFA-A and NCA after 100 cycles.

According to the document, NFA-A retained ≈80% capacity after 100 cycles, while NCA retained ≈68% capacity after 100 cycles.

The percentage by which NFA-A fell behind NCA after 100 cycles can be calculated as follows:

Percentage by which NFA-A fell behind NCA = (Capacity retention of NCA - Capacity retention of NFA-A) / Capacity retention of NCA × 100
= (68% - 80%) / 68% × 100
= -12% / 68% × 100
= -17.65%

However, since we are interested in the percentage by which NFA-A fell behind NCA, we take the absolute value of the result:

Percentage by which NFA-A fell behind NCA = 17.65%
